sources.quote: According to Debtwire, 54 of the 115 companies with liabilities of $1 billion or more were litigated in the Southern District. By contrast, only 27 such businesses filed their Chapter 11s in Delaware during that period.
sources.searcher_note: Disagrees with the lead: Debtwire counts Houston (SDTX) ahead of Delaware on $1B+ cases. Threshold is liabilities, not assets; the period is the Houston boom before the Oct 2023 Jones scandal, not stated as exact years. Same article says Delaware led 8 to 7 in the year after Jones resigned.

sources.quote: The most common venues for bankruptcies continued to be Delaware and the Southern District of Texas, accounting for 40% and 24%, respectively, over the past 12 months.
sources.searcher_note: Public-company Chapter 11 venue shares for a 12-month window ending mid-2025; all public-company filings, not only the $1B+ mega cases (32 mega cases in that window).

sources.quote: Its 47 cases account for approximately 39% of the 120 megacase total through August of this year.
sources.searcher_note: Delaware leads megacases Jan-Aug 2023, but megacase here means $50M+ assets, not $1B+.

sources.quote: In the last 20 years, more than 70 percent of public companies with at least $100 million in assets filed for bankruptcy in a district outside of the one closest to their headquarters
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff venue-shopping piece naming Delaware, SDTX and SDNY as the usual venues; no Delaware-specific counts. Date is the July 2026 issue as read by WebFetch (day not given). Quote sits in a footnote citing a Senate press release.

notes: No source found giving Delaware 46 of 80 $1B+ asset Chapter 11 families since 2015. The closest $1B+ comparison (Debtwire via Texas Lawbook) goes the other way for the Houston-boom years: SDTX 54 of 115 vs Delaware 27, by liabilities. Other coverage uses different thresholds ($50M+ megacases, all public companies) or short windows. Venue shopping itself is widely covered. Nothing found on Houston's 20+-affiliate families showing under $1M assets. Search 1 ran four internal searches in the tool; logged as one query. Snippets (not fetched) say Bloomberg Law and Thomas H. Curran Associates reported Texas large filings rising from 18 in 2024 to 33 in 2025.
